claim: Supersedes the observer-mechanism portion of lesson_4a711949b3ed while preserving its provenance finding. The final MiniGraph reconciliation is not 'asteps() is the sole scheduler plus callbacks over asteps()'. Current perpetua-core PR #1 has one private scheduler, CompiledGraph._run(), yielding a state-bearing execution record; ainvoke() and asteps() are projections over that scheduler. The correct architecture promotes the rich record into an intentional GraphObservation(event, state, optional node delta) seam for trusted in-process consumers, while GraphEvent remains a sanitized control-only projection for streaming/API/UI. A plugin-layer dispatcher drains GraphObservation once and pushes each observation to N GraphPlugin listeners in deterministic registration order, so a checkpointer, tracer, audit hook, and interrupt observer can all observe one run without racing a single async generator. This preserves the 05-feasibility-review.md GraphPlugin groundwork and the one-scheduler invariant simultaneously. The older orama v2 pattern-mining library is evidence beneath the canonical reconciliation rather than superseded history: LangGraph checkpoint/session/reducer ideas feed durability and R3/R4; Pydantic AI tool-schema extraction survives in the generic tool layer without its runtime; Karpathy March-of-Nines becomes evaluator/verification doctrine above the kernel; Swarm/CrewAI/AutoGen map to edges/subgraphs/bounded topology; Foundry evaluation/isolation/routing split across evaluator, effect/security policy, and runtime/GraphSpec layers.

decisions.notes: Direct operator instruction to update PT .agent main after verifying the orama pattern library, GraphPlugin provenance, and actual perpetua-core PR #1 scheduler implementation.
